title: reduce-int8-kernel-latency-with-prefetch-tiler-and-dequant-merge
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Reduce 95th/99th percentile token latency for INT8-heavy workloads while preserving deterministic fallback to FP8 and maintaining KV cache alignment for continuous batching. This PR introduces a tile-prefetch microkernel for int8 GEMM, an upstream dequant-fusion stage integrated into the runtime scheduler, and KV-cache alignment tweaks to avoid extra copies during continuous batching. Changes were iterated against the microbench harness and live canary traffic on a small dedicated pool. Summary of changes: 1) New microkernel redwood/runtime/kernel/int8_tile_prefetch.cpp and supporting headers. The kernel implements per-tile prefetch + intrinsics-friendly data layout for 8-bit matmuls with optional per-head requant hinting. 2) Scheduler integration redwood/runtime/scheduler/prefetch_tiler_scheduler.cc that exposes a tiler policy to the request router and merges the dequant fusion pass into the late scheduling stage so fused dequant+gemm can be scheduled on tile-prefetch capable devices. 3) KV cache alignment adjustments redwood/runtime/cache/kv_alignment.h and KV copy-path optimizations redwood/runtime/cache/kv_continuous_batch.cc to avoid unaligned writes that previously forced extra allocations at end-of-sequence. 4) A runtime config flag (runtime.config.quant.prefer_prefetch) and a safety gate that automatically falls back to the previous path when microkernel returns an unsupported status. 5) Bench harness updates and new unit/integration tests under redwood/tests/quant_perf and perf artifacts under redwood/benchmarks/ci. Benchmarks: On internal microbench suite with sequence lengths 128/256 and batch sizes 1-8 we saw median token latency drop 12%-20% and p99 drop 18%-26% for INT8 pipelines on A100-like devices when using the prefetch tiler; CPU-bound quant paths show no regression. KV continuous-batching scenarios improved throughput by up to 9% due to elimination of one copy per request. Compatibility and risk: The change introduces a non-default config flag and is guarded by hardware capability checks; default behavior unchanged until flag enabled on canary pools. The dequant fusion stage is conservative and preserves numerical equivalence within existing quantization tolerances. Rollout plan: enable on internal perf canary for 48h, monitor token-level latencies and quality metrics, then progressive rollout to dedicated pools. Related: touches scheduling, kernel, and cache subsystems; coordinate with infra and SRE for canary. See linked linear items for profiling runs and rollout checklist.

release_notes: Performance: Introduces optional INT8 tile-prefetch microkernel that reduces token latency and improves continuous-batching throughput when enabled; adds conservative dequant fusion into the scheduler to co-locate dequant+GEMM on prefetch-capable devices. Rollout: feature gated via runtime.config.quant.prefer_prefetch and rolled out gradually to canary pools. No behavioral breaking changes expected.
